patch.summary: Change a user's role or active state (admins; moderators may only suspend or reinstate members)
patch.description: Deactivating a user signs them out everywhere. A real suspension or reinstatement (is_active changing value) also emails the member at their stored address, after the change is saved; the email does not say who acted. Role changes and updates that change nothing send no email. Admins cannot demote or deactivate themselves. Moderators may send only is_active, and only for accounts whose role is user; they cannot change roles (sending the role a member already has is accepted and changes nothing) or touch admins, other moderators or themselves.

403.description: Admins and moderators only, or the target is not allowed (own account, or a moderator changing a role, or acting on an admin or moderator).

delete.description: Admins cannot delete themselves. The account, its stored avatar file and everything it owns are removed.

get.summary: List what staff did (admins only, read-only)
get.description: Newest first. Each entry has id, action, actor {id, name, username, role}, subject {type, id, label}, changes and created_at. The actor's role and the subject's label are the ones recorded at the time; actor id, name and username are null once that account is deleted, and the label keeps a deleted subject readable. changes maps each changed field to {from, to} (role, is_active, status of a review, movie fields); an overview is only marked {changed: true}; a review decision also carries reports_resolved, the number of open reports it closed; it is null when there is nothing to compare (deletions). A movie's subject id is its tmdb_id. Only the changes that went through are recorded: an update that changes nothing records nothing, and neither does approving or rejecting a review whose status stays the same and that had no open reports. Rows are never changed or removed.

parameters.name: subject_id
parameters.description: A user id, review id or movie tmdb_id, depending on subject_type.
